newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Plock refinery to lift petrol prices.
newsitem.headline: Polish Plock refinery to lift petrol prices.

text.p: Poland's largest oil refinery, the state-owned Petrochemia Plock SA, wants to increase prices of fuel by between 10 and 12 percent in March, the firm's press office said on Thursday.
It said that last month Plock had asked the treasury office to clear the rise, as required by the law, but that the office turned down the request.

"In this situation, the law allows us to introduce the increase three months after the treasury office's decision, even though it was negative...The rise will take place in March," an office's spokeswoman told Reuters.
She said the increase was necessary because of growing production costs and high world oil prices.

Poland has promised the European Union to free domestically produced petrol prices, whose maximum levels are now set by the finance minister, by July this year. There are no caps on prices of imported petrol.
Plock, which processes some 10 million tonnes of oil annually, produces about 70 percent of liquid fuels in Poland.
